name: Strange Machines
author: Multiverse Video editors
description: Make unusual physical things and understand how they work.

items.note: A hackerspace workshop on hardware hacking for absolute beginners: how to open a device, find its debug ports, and learn what's inside.
Lessons from building a networking stack for microcontrollers with 32 kB of RAM, in Go.
Nathan Proctor of the US PIRG on the right-to-repair fight and how copyright law (the DMCA) gets used to stop you fixing your own things.
Crowd Supply's Teardown Sessions talks with Michael Altfield, maker of BusKill, a laptop kill-cord, about practical OpSec and privacy hardware.
Two minutes from unboxing to running code: installing MicroPython on a tiny ESP32-C3 board.
Veronica Explains pushes back on tech's habit of shaming people's hardware and software choices: your tools are probably fine.
A Hackerspace Brussels talk on using free software to build your own autonomous robots.
Planning an ESP32 project end to end and connecting it to Wi-Fi with MicroPython, including the parts that don't work the first time.
A walk through an EDM power-supply circuit, explaining how each section works and where it could fail.
An honest DIY test: can one solar panel on a shed roof run a home server rack, or does it just cost money?
A talk on 3D printing with mycelium: growing structures from fungus instead of plastic.
A 2024 demo that squeezes astonishing effects out of a stock 8 MHz Atari STE: the demoscene's art of doing impossible things with old hardware.
A step-by-step solve of a crackmes.one reverse-engineering challenge, narrated so you can follow the reasoning, not just the answer.
A Stargate-inspired 'Dial-Home Device' built from scratch: a beautifully unnecessary machine, documented build step by build step.
